vsm2.13:13.1: Herein, to the knowledge of recollection of past lives means for knowledge concerning recollection of past lives.
vsm2.13:13.2: Past lives is aggregates lived in the past in former births.
vsm2.13:13.3:
“Lived” in that case means lived out, undergone, arisen and ceased in one’s own subjective
continuity. Or alternatively, past lives is mental objects lived in the past in one’s former births;
vsm2.13:13.4:
and “lived” in that case means lived by living in one’s objective resort, which has been cognized and delimited by one’s
own consciousness, or cognized by another’s consciousness, too. In the case of recollection of those past Enlightened
Ones who have broken the cycle, and so on, these last are only accessible to Enlightened Ones.
vsm2.13:13.5:
Recollection of past lives: the mindfulness (memory) by means of which he recollects
the past lives is the recollection of past lives.
vsm2.13:13.6: Knowledge is the knowledge associated with that mindfulness.
vsm2.13:13.7:
To the knowledge of recollection of past lives: for the purpose of the knowledge of the recollection of past
lives in this way; for the attaining, for the reaching, of that knowledge, is what is meant.
vsm2.13:14.1: Manifold: of many kinds: or that has occurred in many ways. Given in detail, is the meaning.
vsm2.13:14.2: Past lives is the continuity lived here and there, taking the immediately previous existence as the beginning and working backwards.
vsm2.13:14.3: He recollects: he recalls it, following it out by the succession of aggregates, or by death and rebirth-linking.
vsm2.13:15.1:
There are six kinds of people who recollect these past lives. They are: other sectarians,
ordinary disciples, great disciples, chief disciples, Paccekabuddhas, and Buddhas.
vsm2.13:16.1: Herein, other sectarians recollect only as far back as forty eons, but not beyond that.
vsm2.13:16.2: Why? Because their understanding is weak
vsm2.13:16.3: for lack of delimitation of mind and matter (see Ch. XVIII).
vsm2.13:16.4: Ordinary disciples recollect as far back as a hundred eons and as far back as a thousand eons because their understanding is strong.
vsm2.13:16.5: The eighty great disciples recollect as far back as a hundred thousand eons.
vsm2.13:16.6: The two chief disciples recollect as far back as an incalculable age and a hundred thousand eons.
vsm2.13:16.7: Paccekabuddhas recollect as far back as two incalculable ages and a hundred thousand eons.
vsm2.13:16.8: For such is the extent to which they can convey their minds back respectively.
vsm2.13:16.9: But there is no limit in the case of Buddhas.
vsm2.13:17.1:
Again, other sectarians only recollect the succession of aggregates; they are unable to recollect
according only to death and rebirth-linking, letting go of the succession of aggregates.
vsm2.13:17.2: They are like the blind in that they are unable to descend upon any place they choose;
vsm2.13:17.3: they go as the blind do without letting go of their sticks. So they recollect without letting go of the succession of aggregates.
vsm2.13:17.4: Ordinary disciples both recollect by means of the succession of aggregates and trace by means of death and rebirth-linking.
vsm2.13:17.6: But the chief disciples have nothing to do with the succession of aggregates.
vsm2.13:17.7:
When they see the death of one person, they see the rebirth-linking, and again when they see the death of another,
they see the rebirth-linking. So they go by tracing through death and rebirth-thinking.
vsm2.13:18.1: Buddhas, however, have nothing to do either with succession of aggregates or with tracing through death and rebirth-linking;
vsm2.13:18.2: for whatever instance they choose in many millions of eons, or more or less, is evident to them.
vsm2.13:18.3:
So they go, and so they descend with the lion’s descent wherever they want, even skipping
over many millions of eons as though they were an elision in a text.
vsm2.13:18.4:
And just as an arrow shot by such a master of archery expert in hair-splitting as Sarabhaṅga (see J-a V 129) always hits
the target without getting held up among trees, creepers, etc., on its way, and so neither gets held up nor misses,
vsm2.13:18.5:
so too, since Buddhas go in this way their knowledge does not get held up in intermediate births or miss;
without getting held up or missing, it seizes any instance required.
vsm2.13:19.1: Among these beings with recollection of past lives, the sectarians’ vision of past lives seems like the light of a glow-worm,
vsm2.13:19.2: that of ordinary disciples like the light of a candle,
vsm2.13:19.3: that of the great disciples like the light of a torch,
vsm2.13:19.4: that of the chief disciples like the light of the morning star,
vsm2.13:19.5: that of Paccekabuddhas like the light of the moon,
vsm2.13:19.6: and that of Buddhas like the glorious autumn sun’s disk with its thousand rays.
vsm2.13:20.1: Other sectarians see past lives as blind men go tapping with the point of a stick.
vsm2.13:20.2: Ordinary disciples do so as men who go on a log bridge.
vsm2.13:20.3: The great disciples do so as men who go on a foot bridge.
vsm2.13:20.4: The chief disciples do so as men who go on a cart bridge.
vsm2.13:20.5: Paccekabuddhas do so as men who go on a main foot-path.
vsm2.13:20.6: And Buddhas do so as men who go on a high road for carts.
vsm2.13:21.1: In this connection it is the disciples’ recollection of past lives that is intended.
vsm2.13:21.2:
Hence it was said above: “‘He recollects’: he recollects it following it
out by the succession of aggregates, or by death and rebirth-linking” (§14).
vsm2.13:22.1:
So a bhikkhu who is a beginner and wants to recollect in this way should go into solitary retreat on return from his alms
round after his meal. Then he should attain the four jhānas in succession and emerge from the fourth jhāna
as basis for direct-knowledge. He should then advert to his most recent act of sitting down for this purpose,
vsm2.13:22.2:
next, to the preparation of the seat, to the entry into the lodging, to the putting away of the bowl and outer
robe, to the time of eating, to the time of returning from the village,
vsm2.13:22.3:
to the time of wandering for alms in the village, to the time of entering the village, to the time of setting
out from the monastery, to the time of paying homage at the shrine terrace and the Enlightenment-tree terrace,
vsm2.13:22.4:
to the time of washing the bowl, to the time of picking up the bowl, to the things
done from the time of picking up the bowl back to the mouth washing,
vsm2.13:22.5:
to the things done in the early morning, to the things done in the middle watch, in the first watch. In this
way he should advert to all the things done during the whole night and day in reverse order.
vsm2.13:23.1:
While this much, however, is evident even to his normal consciousness,
it is especially evident to his preliminary-work consciousness.
vsm2.13:23.2: But if anything there is not evident, he should again attain the basic jhāna, emerge and advert.
vsm2.13:23.3: By so doing it becomes as evident as when a lamp is lit.
vsm2.13:23.4:
And so, in reverse order too, he should advert to the things done on the second day back, and on the third,
fourth and fifth day, and in the ten days, and in the fortnight, and as far back as a year.
vsm2.13:24.1:
When by these means he adverts to ten years, twenty years, and so on as far back as his own rebirth-linking in this existence,
he should advert to the mentality-materiality occurring at the moment of death in the preceding existence;
vsm2.13:24.2:
for a wise bhikkhu is able at the first attempt to remove the rebirth-linking and make
the mentality-materiality at the death moment his object.
vsm2.13:25.1:
But the mentality-materiality in the previous existence has ceased without remainder and another has arisen, and consequently
that instance is, as it were, shut away in darkness, and it is hard for one of little understanding to see it.
vsm2.13:25.2:
Still he should not give up the task, thinking, “I am unable to remove the rebirth-linking and make
the mentality-materiality that occurred at the death moment my object.”
vsm2.13:25.3: On the contrary, he should again and again attain that same basic jhāna, and each time he emerges he should advert to that instance.
vsm2.13:26.2: and when the axe again gets blunt, he does as before and continues chopping it;
vsm2.13:26.3:
and as he goes on chopping it in this way, the tree falls at length, because each time there is no need to chop
again what has already been chopped and what has not yet been chopped gets chopped;
vsm2.13:26.4:
so too, when he emerges from the basic jhāna, instead of adverting to what he has already adverted to, he
should advert only to the rebirth-linking, and at length he removes the rebirth-linking and makes
the mentality-materiality that occurred at the death moment his object.
vsm2.13:26.5: And this meaning should also be illustrated by means of the wood cutter and the hair-cutter as well.
vsm2.13:27.1:
Herein, the knowledge that occurs making its object the period from the last sitting down for this purpose
back to the rebirth-linking is not called knowledge of recollection of past lives;
vsm2.13:27.2: but it is called preliminary-work-concentration knowledge;
vsm2.13:27.3: and some call it “knowledge of the past” (atītaṃsa-ñāṇa), but that is inappropriate to the fine-material sphere.
vsm2.13:27.4:
However, when this bhikkhu has got back beyond the rebirth-linking, there arises in him mind-door
adverting making its object the mentality-materiality that occurred at the death moment.
vsm2.13:27.5: And when that has ceased, then either four or five impulsions impel making that their object too.
vsm2.13:27.6: The first of these, called “preliminary-work,” etc., in the way already described (§5), are of the sense sphere.
vsm2.13:27.7: The last is a fine-material absorption consciousness of the fourth jhāna.
vsm2.13:27.8: The knowledge that arises in him then together with that consciousness is what is called, “knowledge of recollection of past lives.”
vsm2.13:27.9: It is with the mindfulness (memory) associated with that knowledge that he “recollects his manifold past lives,
vsm2.13:27.10: that is to say, one birth, two births, …” thus with details and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives (D I 81).
vsm2.13:28.1: Herein, one birth is the continuity of aggregates included in a single becoming starting with rebirth-linking and ending with death.
vsm2.13:28.2: So too with two births, and the rest.
vsm2.13:28.3:
But in the case of many eons of world contraction, etc., it should be understood that the aeon of world
contraction is an aeon of diminution and the aeon of world expansion is an aeon of increase.
vsm2.13:29.1: Herein, what supersedes the contraction is included in the contraction since it is rooted in it;
vsm2.13:29.2: and so too what supersedes the expansion is included in the expansion. This being so, it includes what is stated thus:
vsm2.13:29.3: “Bhikkhus, there are four incalculables of the aeon. What four?
vsm2.13:29.4: The contraction, what supersedes the contraction, the expansion, and what supersedes the expansion” (A II 142 abbreviated).
vsm2.13:30.1:
Herein, there are three kinds of contraction: contraction due to water,
contraction due to fire, and contraction due to air (see MN 28).
vsm2.13:30.2:
Also there are three limits to the contraction; the Ābhassara (Streaming-radiance) Brahmā-world,
that of the Subhakiṇha (Refulgent-glory), and that of the Vehapphala (Great-fruit).
vsm2.13:30.3: When the aeon contracts owing to fire, all below the Ābhassara Brahmā-world is burnt up by fire.
vsm2.13:30.4: When it contracts owing to water, it is all dissolved by water up to the Subhakiṇha Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:30.5: When it contracts owing to air, it is all demolished by wind up to the Vehapphala Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:31.1: In breadth it is always one of the Buddha-fields that is destroyed.
vsm2.13:31.2: For the Buddha-fields are of three kinds, that is, the field of birth, the field of authority, and the field of scope.
vsm2.13:31.3:
Herein, the field of birth is limited by the ten thousand world-spheres
that quaked on the Perfect One’s taking rebirth-linking, and so on.
vsm2.13:31.4:
The field of authority is limited by the hundred thousand million world-spheres where the following safeguards
(paritta) are efficacious, that is, the Ratana Sutta (Sn p.39), the Khandha Paritta (Vin II 109; A II 72),
the Dhajagga Paritta (S I 218), the Āṭānāṭiya Paritta (D III 194), and the Mora Paritta (J-a II 33).
vsm2.13:31.5: The field of scope is boundless, immeasurable:
vsm2.13:31.6: “As far as he wishes” (A I 228), it is said. The Perfect One knows anything anywhere that he wishes.
vsm2.13:31.7: So one of these three Buddha-fields, that is to say, the field of authority is destroyed.
vsm2.13:31.8: But when that is being destroyed, the field of birth also gets destroyed.
vsm2.13:31.9: And that happens simultaneously; and when it is reconstituted, that happens simultaneously (cf. M-a IV 114).
vsm2.13:32.1: Now, it should be understood how its destruction and reconstitution come about thus.
vsm2.13:32.2:
On the occasion when the aeon is destroyed by fire first of all a great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction
appears, and there is a great downpour all over the hundred thousand million world-spheres.
vsm2.13:32.3: People are delighted, and they bring out all their seeds and sow them.
vsm2.13:32.4:
But when the sprouts have grown enough for an ox to graze, then not a drop of rain falls
any more even when the asses bray. Rain is withheld from then on.
vsm2.13:32.5:
This is what the Blessed One referred to when he said: “Bhikkhus, an occasion comes when for many years, for many
hundreds of years, for many thousands of years, for many hundreds of thousands of years, there is no rain” (A IV 100).
vsm2.13:32.6: Beings that live by rain die and are reborn in the Brahmā-world, and so are the deities that live on flowers and fruits.
vsm2.13:33.1: When a long period has passed in this way, the water gives out here and there.
vsm2.13:33.2: Then in due course the fishes and turtles die and are reborn in the Brahmā-world, and so are the beings in hell.
vsm2.13:33.3: Some say that the denizens of hell perish there with the appearance of the seventh sun (§41).
vsm2.13:33.4:
Now, there is no rebirth in the Brahmā-world without jhāna; and some of them,
being obsessed with the scarcity of food, are unable to attain jhāna, so how are they reborn there?
vsm2.13:33.5: By means of jhāna obtained in the sense-sphere divine world.
vsm2.13:34.1:
For then the sense-sphere deities called world-marshal (loka-byūha) deities come to know that at the end of a hundred
thousand years there will be the emergence of an aeon, and they travel up and down the haunts of men,
their heads bared, their hair dishevelled, with piteous faces, mopping their tears with their hands,
clothed in dyed cloth, and wearing their dress in great disorder. They make this announcement:
vsm2.13:34.2:
“Good sirs, good sirs, at the end of a hundred thousand years from now there will be the emergence of an aeon.
This world will be destroyed. Even the ocean will dry up.
vsm2.13:34.3:
This great earth, and the Sineru King of Mountains, will be consumed and destroyed.
The destruction of the earth will extend as far as the Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:34.4:
Develop loving-kindness, good sirs, develop compassion, gladness, equanimity, good sirs.
Care for your mothers, care for your fathers, honour the elders of your clans.”
vsm2.13:35.1:
When human beings and earth deities hear their words, they mostly are filled with a sense of urgency.
They become kind to each other and make merit with loving-kindness, etc., and so they are reborn in the divine world.
vsm2.13:35.2: There they eat divine food, and they do the preliminary work on the air kasiṇa and acquire jhāna.
vsm2.13:35.3: Others, however, are reborn in a sense-sphere divine world through kamma to be experienced in a future life.
vsm2.13:35.4: For there is no being traversing the round of rebirths who is destitute of kamma to be experienced in a future life.
vsm2.13:35.5: They too acquire jhāna there in the same way.
vsm2.13:35.6: All are eventually reborn in the Brahmā-world by acquiring jhāna in a sense-sphere divine world in this way.
vsm2.13:36.1: However, at the end of a long period after the withholding of the rain, a second sun appears.
vsm2.13:36.2:
And this is described by the Blessed One in the way beginning, “Bhikkhus, there is the occasion
when …” (A IV 100), and the Sattasuriya Sutta should be given in full.
vsm2.13:36.3: Now, when that has appeared, there is no more telling night from day;
vsm2.13:36.4: as one sun sets, the other rises.
vsm2.13:36.5: The world is uninterruptedly scorched by the suns.
vsm2.13:36.6: But there is no sun deity in the aeon-destruction sun as there is in the ordinary sun.
vsm2.13:36.7: Now, when the ordinary sun is present, thunder clouds and mare’s-tail vapours cross the skies.
vsm2.13:36.8: But when the aeon-destruction sun is present, the sky is as blank as the disk of a looking-glass and destitute of clouds and vapour.
vsm2.13:36.9: Beginning with the rivulet, the water in all the rivers except the five great rivers dries up.
vsm2.13:37.1: After that, at the end of a long period, a third sun appears. And when that has appeared, the great rivers dry up too.
vsm2.13:38.1: After that, at the end of a long period, a fourth sun appears.
vsm2.13:38.2:
And when that has appeared, the seven great lakes in Himalaya, the sources of the great rivers, dry up,
that is to say: Sīhapapāta, Haṃsapātana, Kaṇṇamuṇḍaka, Rathakāra, Anotatta, Chaddanta, and Kuṇāla.
vsm2.13:39.1:
After that, at the end of a long period, a fifth sun appears, and when that has appeared,
there eventually comes to be not enough water left in the great ocean to wet one finger joint.
vsm2.13:40.1: After that, at the end of a long period, a sixth sun appears,
vsm2.13:40.2: and when that has appeared, the whole world-sphere becomes nothing but vapour, all its moisture being evaporated.
vsm2.13:40.3: And the hundred thousand million world-spheres are the same as this one.
